definitions.question: Two simultaneous operations on one business object must be explainable by one legal sequential history.
Two actors cannot both pass the same stale precondition and create mutually inconsistent final states.
Concurrent read-check-write paths must not lose a committed update or duplicate a one-time entitlement.
Concurrent capture/cancel/refund/claim operations must converge on one authoritative effect order.

definitions.group: BRANCH 50 — Atomic transaction / authoritative commit point
definitions.question: Every externally visible business transition has one authoritative commit/effect point.

definitions.group: BRANCH 50 — Atomic transaction / authoritative commit point
definitions.question: A pre-commit response, redirect, modal, or local status cannot be mistaken for committed finality.

definitions.group: BRANCH 50 — Atomic transaction / authoritative commit point
definitions.question: A post-commit retry cannot create a second economic or entitlement effect.

definitions.group: BRANCH 50 — Atomic transaction / authoritative commit point
definitions.question: Different channels reporting the same event must bind to the same committed transaction identity.
Two transactions that each satisfy local predicates must not jointly violate a cross-object invariant.
Eligibility/ownership/limit decisions must not rely on a snapshot older than a conflicting committed change.
A phantom/new row or object cannot make a previously checked quota/uniqueness predicate false at commit.
Repeated reads inside one logical business decision cannot silently observe incompatible system histories.

definitions.group: BRANCH 52 — TOCTOU / stale precondition / optimistic validation
definitions.question: Authority checked when a UI/control is rendered must still be valid when the state mutation commits.
definitions.method_lineage: Adya; NASA timing/state; Saltzer complete mediation

definitions.group: BRANCH 52 — TOCTOU / stale precondition / optimistic validation
definitions.question: Price/amount/currency/owner checked at request start must be revalidated if mutable before finalization.
definitions.method_lineage: Adya; NASA timing/state; Saltzer complete mediation

definitions.group: BRANCH 52 — TOCTOU / stale precondition / optimistic validation
definitions.question: Consumed eligibility or transferred ownership must invalidate a stale button, token, form, or queued action.
definitions.method_lineage: Adya; NASA timing/state; Saltzer complete mediation

definitions.group: BRANCH 52 — TOCTOU / stale precondition / optimistic validation
definitions.question: An optimistic compare-and-swap/version check must fail rather than overwrite a newer valid business state.
definitions.method_lineage: Adya; NASA timing/state; Saltzer complete mediation

definitions.question: Duplicate delivery of the same webhook/event/message produces at most one business effect.
definitions.method_lineage: Lamport temporal reasoning; distributed transaction methods

definitions.question: Out-of-order delivery cannot regress a terminal state or reverse a later authoritative transition.
definitions.method_lineage: Lamport temporal reasoning; distributed transaction methods

definitions.question: A missing message can be reconciled from the system of record without synthesizing a new economic event.
definitions.method_lineage: Lamport temporal reasoning; distributed transaction methods

definitions.question: A delayed message cannot resurrect an expired/cancelled/consumed object without a new authorized transition.
definitions.method_lineage: Lamport temporal reasoning; distributed transaction methods

definitions.group: BRANCH 54 — Causal order / happens-before / monotonic observation
definitions.question: A child/follow-up event cannot finalize before the parent event it causally depends on exists.

definitions.group: BRANCH 54 — Causal order / happens-before / monotonic observation
definitions.question: A derived transaction must bind to the exact version/state of the parent that authorized it.

definitions.group: BRANCH 54 — Causal order / happens-before / monotonic observation
definitions.question: Reverse arrival order must be queued/reconciled rather than classified as independent valid events.

definitions.group: BRANCH 54 — Causal order / happens-before / monotonic observation
definitions.question: A user or controller that observes a later terminal state must not subsequently observe an older conflicting state as current.
Two partitions updating one logical object must reconcile without duplicate value or lost authority metadata.
Conflict resolution must preserve canonical owner/finality rather than choose the last visible wrapper.
An offline/stale action replayed after reconnection must revalidate against current authoritative state.
Merge logic must not equate two economic events merely because visible amount/label/recipient matches.
Every valid initiated workflow can eventually reach success, explicit failure, cancellation, or another defined terminal state.
definitions.method_lineage: Lamport TLA+; van der Aalst workflow soundness

definitions.question: Funds/reservations/credits/holds cannot remain permanently stranded in an intermediate state without a recovery path.
definitions.method_lineage: Lamport TLA+; van der Aalst workflow soundness

definitions.question: Every reachable intermediate state has at least one valid route to terminal resolution or explicit human escalation.
definitions.method_lineage: Lamport TLA+; van der Aalst workflow soundness

definitions.question: A retry/recovery loop cannot run indefinitely while producing no state progress.
definitions.method_lineage: Lamport TLA+; van der Aalst workflow soundness

definitions.question: An eligible work item that remains enabled cannot be perpetually skipped by the scheduler/queue.
Priority policy must not indefinitely starve a role, market, payment method, merchant, or error class that remains valid.
Backoff/retry logic must not make eventual processing impossible for a persistently valid item.
Human and automated paths must not create an unbounded fairness gap when both satisfy the same governing eligibility rule.
From every reachable workflow state, the intended terminal state remains reachable.
When a case terminates, no stale active token/hold/reservation/pending task remains outside the terminal object.
No required transition/task is structurally dead across all valid routes.
A single logical case cannot finish with two incompatible terminal artifacts or statuses.
An AND-join finalizes only after every required prerequisite branch has completed.
An OR/choice branch cannot be treated as if all branches completed or vice versa.
Failure of one required parallel branch cannot silently produce whole-workflow success.
Duplicate tokens/branch completions cannot trigger the join/finalizer more than once.
Each condition in an eligibility/authorization decision can independently change the final decision when other relevant conditions are held fixed.
A condition masked by short-circuit/default logic is identified instead of assumed tested.
Every decision outcome and every condition true/false state has a valid specimen or explicit impossibility reason.
A duplicated/redundant condition cannot hide a missing required predicate behind an apparently equivalent branch.
Pairwise actor/role × channel combinations preserve the same governing invariant where equivalence is required.
Three-way role × lifecycle-state × software/config-version combinations are covered for high-value finalizers.
Money paths cover constrained combinations such as currency × payment method × market × reversal state without illegal cross-products.
Higher-strength t-way coverage is applied only around critical/finality predicates where lower-strength coverage leaves plausible interaction gaps.
The same valid events in a different order cannot create an unauthorized final state.
definitions.method_lineage: NIST ordered t-way state-based testing; Lamport

definitions.question: Repeating one legal subsequence cannot create an extra final/economic consequence.
definitions.method_lineage: NIST ordered t-way state-based testing; Lamport

definitions.question: Omitting an intermediate event cannot cause a later transition to inherit authority it never received.
definitions.method_lineage: NIST ordered t-way state-based testing; Lamport

definitions.question: A delayed terminal event following a newer terminal event cannot overwrite the authoritative final state.
definitions.method_lineage: NIST ordered t-way state-based testing; Lamport

definitions.question: Generate only business objects/states that satisfy declared type and precondition constraints before testing invariants.
When a property fails, reduce the case to the smallest object/state change that still reproduces the failure.
Shrinking preserves domain legality so a minimal counterexample is not an impossible transaction.
For sequence failures, minimize the transition trace to the smallest causal subsequence that still violates the invariant.
Changing a presentation-only field must not change money, ownership, authority, or finality.
A reversible transformation followed by its inverse must return to the same authoritative business state when no external event intervenes.
Equivalent channels/routes must preserve the same invariant even when exact expected output is unknown.
Permutation of an unordered input set or addition of irrelevant metadata must not change a decision unless the governing rule names that field.
Every read/mutate/finalize path checks the current authority for the exact object.
Cached/prevalidated/internal paths do not bypass the final authority check.
Admin/support/API/batch routes enforce the same object boundary unless a separately owned authority explicitly permits otherwise.
A new entry point or legacy path cannot inherit permission merely because another route already mediated the object.
Unknown/missing state cannot default to a finalizing side effect.
Timeout/parser/provider/config errors do not grant access, credit, refund, or approval.
Missing rule/configuration selects quarantine/deny/review rather than the broadest permission.
Exception/fallback branches preserve the same authorization and amount limits as the happy path.
Each role/service account possesses only the privileges needed for its business function.
Read/export authority does not imply mutation/finalization authority.
Support/operations roles cannot silently exercise merchant/customer ownership rights.
Cross-tenant/service credentials are scoped to the exact merchant/account/object instead of broad ambient access.
Where dual control is part of the business invariant, one principal cannot both originate and independently approve the protected action.
Delegation/subdelegation cannot collapse two required independent authorities into one effective principal.
Override/high-impact finalization requires every independent predicate/key intended by policy.
Automation does not accidentally merge maker/checker roles that are separated on the human path.

definitions.question: A service/deputy uses the caller/object-specific authority for caller-directed work instead of its own broader ambient authority.
A user-controlled identifier/return target cannot cause a privileged service to operate on a different protected object.
Support/admin actions bind requester identity, target owner, and authority source rather than only a target identifier.
A delegated token/capability cannot be repurposed for an object/action outside the authority embedded in that delegation.
Protected business objects change only through an authorized transformation procedure/state transition.
Unconstrained user/external input becomes a validated constrained object or is rejected before finality.
A certified transition starting from a valid state must end in another valid state under every allowed input class.
Direct/manual/legacy writes cannot bypass the transformation procedure that owns integrity.

definitions.group: DP-H — Dynamic revocation + reconstructable integrity audit
definitions.question: Revoked/consumed/transferred authority invalidates already-issued sessions/buttons/tokens before mutation.

definitions.group: DP-H — Dynamic revocation + reconstructable integrity audit
definitions.question: Every protected transformation leaves enough immutable audit data to reconstruct actor, object, authority, before/after state and time.

definitions.group: DP-H — Dynamic revocation + reconstructable integrity audit
definitions.question: Integrity verification can detect a protected object that no longer satisfies its declared business invariant.

definitions.group: DP-H — Dynamic revocation + reconstructable integrity audit
definitions.question: The actor executing a protected transaction cannot silently rewrite the audit evidence needed to review that same transaction.
